clue.text: Ulster, for example, portrayed in outstanding film

parts.note: a film is a thin covering layer, a coat

explanation.surface: Northern Ireland is depicted in a brilliant movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulster' looks like the province, but here it is a long, heavy overcoat named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long loose overcoat, so it is one example of a heavy outdoor garment of this kind.

clue.text: Astronomer sees trail rising over one constellation

indicators.note: in a down entry, something rising is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to trail is to lag behind

explanation.surface: A stargazer watches a path climbing above a group of stars.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' simply places the first pieces above the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian scientist who first turned a telescope on the heavens, a famous astronomer.

clue.text: Rhea spinning, orbiting close to host planet

indicators.note: to orbit something is to circle round it, so one piece goes around the other
spinning things tumble round, so the letters of the name come out in a new order

parts.note: the name taken as letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A spinning moon of Saturn circles near its host planet.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhea is a moon of Saturn, which makes 'planet' feel like part of the scene rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the third planet from the Sun, the world we live on.

clue.text: Gang member, thug, or defter lad possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the words could be made into something else, a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A member of a gang is described as either a brute or a nimbler youth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface names a thug, but the gang is Fagin's band of child pickpockets in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Dawkins, nicknamed the Artful Dodger, is the leading pickpocket in Fagin's gang in Oliver Twist.

clue.text: Article supporting absent king

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes after the other

parts.note: off as in away from work, not present

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece backs a monarch who is away.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famous for the dyke along the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia, so he is a historical English monarch.

clue.text: Road metal, I suspect, is ideal

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious or not straight, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: ten letters to rearrange, the I included

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that crushed stone for road-building is the perfect material.
explanation.walkthrough: Road metal is broken stone used for surfacing roads; the I belongs to the fodder, not the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tailor-made is perfectly fitted to its purpose, which makes it exactly right, or ideal.

clue.text: Harmony — some from us (Icehouse)

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their run of letters is wanted

parts.note: letters running across the words, the M from the tail of the indicator's 'from'

explanation.surface: A band is asked to share some of its tuneful sound.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run actually starts with the last letter of 'from'. Icehouse is an Australian rock band, which gives the brackets their sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmony is used loosely for pleasing combined sound, and so for music itself.

clue.text: Shakespeare character married sisters off swiftly

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or out of kilter, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A character from the plays weds and then the sisters leave in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistress Quickly is the hostess of the Boar's Head tavern in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays and Henry V.

clue.text: Drink? It might kill you

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a mix of lager and cider
second meaning: a venomous wound from a serpent

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a warning about a strong cocktail, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a pub mix of lager and cider, and the venomous wound a serpent can inflict.

clue.text: Continue song and dance

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a fuss or commotion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' is idiom for a fuss, not a performance; the noun form of the phrase means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the phrase means keep going; as a noun it is a fuss or palaver, like a song and dance.

clue.text: Left composer in NI town

parts.note: Thomas Arne, who wrote Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A composer has departed to live in a Northern Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed but is just L. NI is Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Larne is a port town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland, with ferries to Scotland.

clue.text: Appeal for just treatment if a friar's in trouble

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disarray, so its letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A monk who has got into difficulty pleads to be treated justly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock plea that everyone be treated equitably, an appeal for even-handed dealing.

clue.text: Outbreak of cholera — 100 lost here in Pakistan

indicators.note: an outbreak breaks things apart, so the disease's letters scatter into a new order
lost means gone missing, so that number's letter is taken away

explanation.surface: A cholera epidemic kills a hundred people in a Pakistani city.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'here in Pakistan', a place where all this happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is the capital of Punjab province and Pakistan's second-largest city, so a place there.

clue.text: Good manners in palace? Yes, astonishingly

parts.note: a royal court is a palace

indicators.note: something done astonishingly is done in a surprising way, so the letters come out unexpectedly arranged

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed to find good manners at a royal residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtesy is polite, considerate behaviour, the very thing meant by good manners.

clue.text: Disney animation? Not so, a chap broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely like seed, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A man on air denies that a cartoon is what it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Pocahontas is the 1995 Disney animated feature film about the Powhatan woman of that name.

clue.text: Not working, so rep may be this?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: broken down or out of service
second meaning, playful: a sales rep paid by results would be short of earnings on each sale

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: a sales representative earns commission on sales, so one who is not selling is literally without it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means out of service or broken, and literally describes someone deprived of a sales percentage.

clue.text: Animals tense? New baby acts unexpectedly

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh form, so the words that follow get a different arrangement
unexpectedly means not in the order anticipated, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pets get nervous when a newborn behaves surprisingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is part of the newborn picture and doubles up with 'unexpectedly' to signal the rearrangement; it supplies no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabby cats are domestic cats with striped coats, so they are animals.

clue.text: Cockney's Greek dish?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rhyming slang, the dish name rhyming with Greek
second meaning: fried leftover potato and cabbage

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it; the phrase rhyming with Greek is also a traditional British fry-up of leftover potato and cabbage.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is London rhyming slang for a Greek person, and also the name of a fried vegetable dish.

clue.text: Grow a mass of flowers

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the flowers on a tree or bush

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to a gardener, but the verb and the noun phrase are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means develop or flourish; as a noun it is the flowering of a tree, such as cherry.

clue.text: King and Merlin rebuilt citadel

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again differently, so the wizard's letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Arthur and his wizard restore a fortress, a scene from Camelot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the fortified complex in central Moscow; the word itself means a Russian citadel.

clue.text: Prostitute heading off with stupid person, pretty ugly perhaps

indicators.note: with its heading off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: doxy is an old word for a prostitute or mistress

explanation.surface: A streetwalker leaves with a fool, the pair rather unattractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty ugly' looks like a description of the couple, but it is an example of contradictory terms placed together.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxymoron joins contradictory words, as 'pretty' (lovely) set beside 'ugly' does; hence 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Copyright infringer could make publisher's head very annoyed

indicators.note: the head of a word is its beginning, so only its opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: Someone stealing a book could make its publisher furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate illegally copies and sells others' works, infringing their copyright.

clue.text: So long, notice that is put on top of unit

indicators.note: in a down entry, what is put on top comes first when read downwards

parts.note: i.e., Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A farewell note is pinned above a section.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, used in English just like the informal farewell so long.

clue.text: Said of country life all but past

indicators.note: all but means everything except, so one stretch of letters is removed

parts.note: pastoral means relating to rural life

explanation.surface: It is reported that rural life is mostly over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Past' seems to be part of the indicator's sense, but its letters are exactly the ones removed from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written, so an oral statement is one said aloud.

clue.text: Butcher giving amusement after start of sale

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: laughter is a sign of amusement

explanation.surface: A meat seller is giggling once the sale begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' reads as a shopkeeper but is a verb: to kill brutally.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher means to kill savagely and in large numbers, which is to slaughter.

clue.text: What baleen whales eat would make top two in 17 poorly

indicators.note: the top two of a down entry are its first pair of letters

parts.note: the first two letters of the answer to 17 down

explanation.surface: Whale food is said to sit at the top of a sick list.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 refers to the answer at 17 down, KREMLIN, whose opening pair supplies the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Krill are tiny shrimp-like crustaceans that baleen whales filter from seawater as their main food.

clue.text: Skinflint causing endless grief

indicators.note: endless means without an end, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A tightwad brings unending sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint hoards money and hates spending it, exactly what a miser does.

clue.text: Girl on line ordered nun a teacake

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A girl on the phone instructs a nun to have a teacake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as giving an order to the nun, but it signals the nun's letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sally Lunn is a large, light, sweet bun or teacake associated with the city of Bath.
